meta.title: Claims-to-capital operating backbone
meta.note: Every operation carries a level. The claim is about where the line sits, not that it can be removed.

levels.label: Autonomous
levels.definition: Runs without a person in the path. Deterministic, checkable, cheap to re-run. Someone audits the output; nothing waits on them.

levels.label: Human-in-the-loop
levels.definition: The system does the work and proposes a result. A person confirms, corrects or rejects it before anything moves downstream.

levels.label: Human
levels.definition: Stays with a person. The system can assemble the record and lay out the considerations. The judgment and the accountability do not move.

operations.label: Ingest and schema normalization
operations.does: Reads loss runs and register extracts in whatever shape they arrive. Maps them to the program schema and normalizes dates, statuses and coverage codes.
operations.why: Mechanical and fully checkable. The mapping is declared, and every transformation traces back to its source row.

operations.label: Identity and entity resolution
operations.does: Finds the same claim arriving under different numbers, and the same insured under different spellings. Proposes merges.
operations.why: A wrong merge costs as much as a missed duplicate. High recall, no autonomy: every merge waits for a person.

operations.label: Policy year and coverage assignment
operations.does: Assigns each claim to a policy year and coverage part from its dates and the coverage basis.
operations.why: Rule-driven from the policy terms. Claims-made and occurrence are unambiguous once the dates are clean, and cleaning them happens upstream.

operations.label: Coverage issue identification
operations.does: Reads the claim file against the policy form. Surfaces the provisions in play, the facts that bear on them, and the open questions.
operations.why: Finding the relevant provisions is reliable. Weighing them is not. It assembles the file and stops.

operations.label: Coverage determination
operations.does: Decides whether the claim is covered, in part or at all, and on what terms.
operations.why: A coverage position is a legal judgment the carrier will be held to. No efficiency argument should move it.

operations.label: Erosion and development computation
operations.does: Tracks paid and incurred against the per-claim retention and the annual aggregate. Builds the development triangle.
operations.why: Arithmetic on reconciled data. The only failure mode is bad input, which is what the exception gate upstream is for.

operations.label: Case reserve setting
operations.does: Proposes a case reserve from the claim's characteristics and how comparable claims developed.
operations.why: The adjuster knows things the record does not: venue, opposing counsel, how the plaintiff presents. The proposal anchors. The adjuster decides.

operations.label: IBNR and ultimate projection
operations.does: Projects each policy year to ultimate using factors derived from the program's own triangle.
operations.why: Standard method, derived factors. Judgment enters through the tail, which sits on the page as a control instead of inside the code.

operations.label: Funding requirement calculation
operations.does: Converts projected ultimate liabilities and the target margin into a required funding position by quarter.
operations.why: Deterministic once the projection and the margin policy are set. Both are visible and both are adjustable.

operations.label: Funding trigger and capital call
operations.does: Decides whether to call capital, adjust the funding schedule, or restructure at renewal.
operations.why: It moves money and it involves the parent. The system's job is to make the number defensible early, while there is still time to argue about it.

operations.label: Invoice review against billing guidelines
operations.does: Checks counsel invoices line by line against the guidelines: block billing, staffing ratios, rate changes, duplicate entries, non-billable tasks. Proposes the adjustment.
operations.why: Flagging a line against a written rule is mechanical. Short-paying a firm is a contract position and a relationship call. The review runs on every line. The deduction waits.

operations.label: Counsel assignment and strategy
operations.does: Selects counsel and sets litigation strategy and settlement authority.
operations.why: Relationship and judgment. The system can supply the performance data and should not act on it.

operations.label: Board memo drafting
operations.does: Assembles the quarterly capacity memo: position, movement, projection, exceptions. Every figure links to the rows behind it.
operations.why: Assembly is mechanical and the narrative is templated from computed values. A person owns it before it goes out.

operations.label: Board decision
operations.does: Approves the renewal structure, the funding position and the capacity plan.
operations.why: Always. The traceability exists to make this decision better informed, not to relocate it.
